statements.title: Merchant Account Reports
statements.subtitle: Generate, review and publish account statements for merchants.
statements.loadFailed: This couldn’t be loaded. Refresh the page to try again.

generate.heading: Generate a statement
generate.description: Choose a merchant and a reporting period. The statement is saved as a draft that only managers can see — review it, then publish it to the merchant.
generate.timezone: UAE calendar days. A delivery counts on the day it was completed, a return on the day it was returned — not the booking date.

list.heading: Statements
list.empty: No statements yet. Generate one above.

actions.publishDescription: {merchant} will be able to view and download it under Account Reports, and their account users are notified in the app. A published statement can’t be edited — only replaced by a correction.
actions.discardDescription: The draft is deleted. Nothing was shared with the merchant.
actions.correctDescription: A new draft is generated from the current records for the same merchant and period. When you publish it, it replaces this statement, which stays on record marked as superseded.
actions.generatedNotice: Draft generated. Only managers can see it. Check the figures, then publish it to the merchant.
actions.publishedNotice: Published. The merchant can now view and download this statement.
actions.emailMerchant: Also email the merchant that it’s ready. The email links to their dashboard and contains no amounts.

settlement.heading: Payments
settlement.description: Record money paid out to the merchant or received from them for this statement. Payments are never deleted; a wrong one is voided with a reason.
settlement.recordPayout: Record a payment to the merchant
settlement.recordReceipt: Record a payment received from the merchant
settlement.onlyCurrent: This statement was replaced. Record payments on the current statement — payments made here still count towards it.
settlement.voidDescription: The payment stays on record, marked void, and no longer counts towards the balance. The merchant can see that it was voided.

document.title: Merchant Account Statement
document.draftNotice: Draft for review — not yet issued to the merchant. Figures are fixed as generated; publish it to issue it.
document.supersededNotice: This statement was replaced by statement {number} on {date}. It is kept for your records.
document.correctionNotice: This statement corrects and replaces statement {number}. Reason: {reason}

summary.codAlreadyRemitted: Less: COD already paid out to you
summary.paymentsReceived: Add: delivery fees you already paid
summary.cashHandlingFeeVaried: Cash-handling fee (at the rate in force each day; {rate} now, of {base})

notes.heading: How this statement is calculated
notes.basis: Lists every delivery completed and every return made in the period (UAE time), once each. Cancelled and in-progress shipments are not included. All amounts are in UAE Dirhams.
notes.serviceRule: Service charge: the delivery price recorded when the shipment was booked.
notes.returnRule: Return charge: {rate} of the original delivery service cost (the booked price without any cash-on-delivery fee), for returned shipments only.
notes.handlingRule: Cash-handling fee: {rate} of the cash on delivery collected for you, per shipment. It is not charged on delivery fees or prepaid shipments.
notes.paidRule: Delivery fees already paid — in cash to the driver or by card — are credited, so no fee is charged twice.
notes.remittedRule: Cash on delivery already paid out to you is deducted, so it isn’t paid twice.
notes.unverified: {amount} of cash on delivery was marked collected before collections were verified and is not included. ParcelLink will confirm it separately.
notes.uncollected: {amount} of cash on delivery on delivered shipments has no recorded collection yet and is not included.
notes.feesUnverified: {amount} of delivery fees marked paid before collections were verified is not credited here.
notes.pdfCharacters: Some text uses characters this PDF can’t display (shown as ?). The statement in your ParcelLink dashboard shows them in full.
notes.ratesVary: The rates changed during this period. Each shipment is charged at the rate in force on the day it was completed.

document.footer: This statement is generated from ParcelLink’s delivery, cash-on-delivery and payment records. Once issued it doesn’t change; any correction is issued as a new statement.
document.questions: Questions about this statement? Contact {email} or {phone}.

performance.title: Business Performance
performance.loadFailed: The report couldn’t be loaded. Refresh the page to try again.
performance.basis: Accrual basis: revenue is recognised on the day a delivery is completed (or a merchant shipment is returned) and expenses on the day they were incurred, in UAE calendar days. Cash collected on behalf of merchants (COD) is not ParcelLink revenue.

revenue.heading: Revenue
revenue.otherHint: ParcelLink doesn’t record any other revenue source yet.
revenue.counts: {delivered, plural, one {# delivery} other {# deliveries}} completed ({merchant} merchant, {individual} individual & walk-in), {returned} returned.
revenue.codMemoHint: Held for merchants and paid out through their statements — not revenue.

expenses.heading: Expenditure
expenses.official: Official expenses: everything managers record, plus operator expenses in approved reports.
expenses.awaiting: {amount} is awaiting review and not counted yet.

profit.heading: Profitability
profit.description: A management view: each line deducts one more expense group from the line above. These are cumulative steps, not separate definitions of profit.
profit.afterSalary: Profit after fuel, subscription, and salary
profit.afterRent: Profit after fuel, subscription, salary, and rent

breakEven.heading: Break-even
breakEven.notAchieved: ParcelLink needs {amount} more revenue in this period to cover its operating costs.
breakEven.assumption: Treats every recorded expense as a fixed cost of the period. A contribution-margin estimate isn’t shown because ParcelLink doesn’t record variable costs per delivery.

details.heading: Supporting details
details.description: The shipments behind the revenue figures. Open one to see its record; expense totals link to the expenses behind them.
details.none: No deliveries or returns were completed in this period.
details.truncated: Showing the first {shown}. Download the shipments CSV for all of them.

void.description: “{description}” stays on record but stops counting in every total. This can’t be undone.

categories.heading: Categories
categories.description: Each category counts toward one profit step. Add categories any time; they’re never deleted, only deactivated.
categories.name: Name
categories.groupHint: “Other operating” is deducted only in net operating profit.

expenses.officialNote: The totals here are the official expenses: costs managers record, plus operator expenses in approved reports. Operator expenses still in review are on Performance Reports.

rates.heading: Statement rates
rates.description: The return charge rate used on statements and in the performance report. There is no cash-handling charge.
rates.current: In force today: return charge {returnRate} of the original service cost.
rates.hint: Each shipment is charged at the rate in force on the day it was completed, so a new rate never changes statements already issued or earlier periods of the performance report. Rates can start today or later; a rate scheduled for a future day can be replaced until then.
rates.noHandling: There is no cash-handling charge: merchants are billed only the flat delivery rates, and the COD collected for them is paid out in full.

operatorExpenses.title: Expenses
operatorExpenses.subtitle: Record the operational expenses you pay, with a receipt, and send them to a manager in a weekly, monthly or custom report. They count in the business figures once a manager approves the report.
operatorExpenses.addHint: An expense dated in one of your draft or returned reports joins it. A period you have already submitted is closed.
operatorExpenses.prepareHint: Choose a week, a month or a range. Your reports can’t overlap, so each expense is reported once.

review.description: Check the expenses and receipts, then approve the report or return it to the operator.
review.returnDescription: The operator can then correct it and submit it again. Tell them what needs changing.
review.approvalMeaning: Approving confirms the report was reviewed and accepted, and counts it in the business figures. It doesn’t record a payment or reimbursement.
